newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Reuters Poll Trend for Australia - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Reuters Poll Trend for Australia - Nov 28.

text.p: The Reuters Poll Trend shows Australian opinion polls stabilising after three months in which the government steadily opened its already large lead.
The government's trend lead on primary voting intention was about 15 percentage points on the weekend of November 17, unchanged from a fortnight before.
The lead bottomed at about 11 points in August, still well above the 8.5 percentage point gap that delivered the government its landslide election win in March.
The two-party preferred vote -- mimicking outcomes under Australia's preferential voting system -- showed a steady government lead of 14 percentage points on November 17.
Prime Minister John Howard was 32 percentage points ahead of Opposition Leader Kim Beazley as preferred prime minister, again little different from the previous position.

This data, always subject to revision, is more than usually provisional because it lacks results from the McNair poll, which last published data for November 3. This particularly affects the two-party and preferred-PM results.
